_readme: Maps a CoinGecko platform slug to a CAIP-2 chain ID and the CAIP-19 asset namespace used for tokens on it. This file is the ONLY platform truth the build reads; nothing is derived at build time. Confidence: high = exercised in production ingest or ratified by a CASA spec; medium = hand-reviewed against a named source; low = auto name-match or a provisional namespace with no ratified spec. Raising a confidence level or clearing an entry from `unmapped` is the most useful contribution to this repo.

hedera-hashgraph.note: CoinGecko stores the EVM-alias 0x form; the CAIP-19 reference is the shard.realm.num tokenID. Conversion is unresolved — see data/unmapped. CoinGecko publishes chain_identifier 295 (Hedera’s EVM-compatible JSON-RPC layer). We keep the CASA-ratified native identity hedera:mainnet, because CAIP-19 for Hedera is defined there and the token references are HTS token IDs, not EVM contracts. A handful of CoinGecko rows carry a full 20-byte EVM address rather than an HTS long-zero alias or a shard.realm.num token id; those are smart-contract-service tokens, not HTS tokens, and are rejected rather than mis-filed as HTS.

cardano.note: Reference format is CIP-34’s <network-id>-<network-magic>, verified live. The NAMESPACE was changed from the provisional "cip34" to "cardano": CASA names a namespace after the ecosystem, not after a specification document, and the two document-named namespaces (eip155, bip122) bound cross-ecosystem families where no ecosystem name would fit — which is not Cardano’s situation. "cip34:" strings are in real circulation (@dcspark/cip34-js, x402) and remain a recognised legacy alias. Submitted to CASA as the "cardano" namespace.

the-open-network.note: asset_namespace `jetton` IS MY INVENTION -- no spec defines an asset namespace for the tvm namespace. CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION WARNING: the user-friendly TON address form is 48 chars of base64 and the URL-safe variant contains `_` and `-` (sample 2 is EQBT2Ee4Lx5w9uI7oMly5upXNs3ABWL_Fwk1uiM74gZCGaYt, note the `_`). CAIP-19's asset_reference charset is [-.%a-zA-Z0-9], which EXCLUDES `_` and `+` and `/`. So CoinGecko's raw identity cannot be dropped into a CAIP-19 asset_reference verbatim. Options: (a) normalise to URL-safe base64 and percent-encode `_` as %5F, or (b) use the raw form's account-id hex (workchain 0 assumed) e.g. bbae71c7b4c5412b28621a701bb58225cc6c52d1d7e2dd96c7131157d0b622f5, which is charset-clean but drops the workchain and the bounceable/testnet flags. addressFormat `ton-friendly-address` (NEW, for you to implement): 48 chars, base64 or base64url alphabet, first byte encodes flags so the string begins EQ/UQ/kQ/0Q; decodes to 36 bytes = 1 flag byte + 1 signed workchain byte + 32 address bytes + 2-byte CRC16-XMODEM checksum.
